newsitem.title: UK: Prison rules eased for pregnant Irish bomb suspect.
newsitem.headline: Prison rules eased for pregnant Irish bomb suspect.

text.p: British authorities have eased prison conditions for Roisin McAliskey, an expectant mother wanted in Germany in connection with an IRA mortar attack on a British army barracks.

McAliskey, the 25-year-old daughter of veteran Irish nationalist campaigner Bernadette McAliskey, nee Devlin, has had her security classification downgraded and she will not be subjected to frequent strip searches, the Prison Service said.
McAliskey is due to give birth in May and authorities declined to say whether Friday's ruling meant she would be allowed to keep her baby with her in jail.

That would not have been possible under her old status -- Category A High Risk -- imposed after her arrest last November in connection with an IRA attack on a British barracks in Osnabrueck last June.

The IRA called a ceasefire in its battle to oust Britain from Northern Ireland in Agust 1994. The truce was broken 17 months later with a series of attacks on targets in mainland Britain before the Osnabrueck attack.
The Fuascailt (Liberation) Irish Political Prisoners Movement has been campaigning for McAliskey to be released on bail while German authorities seek her extradition.
Britain, which denies it holds any political prisoners, has been holding her in prison because it was felt she was likely to abscond. McAliskey denies involvement in the Osnabrueck attack.
Her supporters say she has been subjected to "barbaric and inhumane conditions" in prison, but the Prison Service says her treatment has been "appropriate and humane".
Bernadette McAliskey welcomed the downgrading of her daughter's security classification as good news but said that since the move acknowledged she was not an escape risk, she should be allowed bail.

"It doesn't change the real nature of the problem. If she's not going to try and escape, she's not going to abscond, so why doesn't she have bail," said Bernadette in a speech to a Fuascailt public meeting in London on Friday.
Challenging the German authorities to "put their charges on the table", she said: "What harm is it doing to anyone if a woman who is seven months pregnant is released on bail."
Bernadette said her daughter would also be allowed into the activity room at Holloway women's prison, where she would be permitted to sew.
"She's now going to be allowed to sew, which is what everyone wants to hear on the eve of international women's day," Bernadette said.
As Bernadette Devlin, Roisin's mother was one of the most prominent Irish nationalists of the 1960s.
She became the youngest woman to be elected to the British parliament when she took her seat on her 22nd birthday in 1969.

That same year she was sentenced to six months in prison for inciting people to riot in the Northern Ireland city of Londonderry. In 1972, she punched the then home secretary (interior minister), Reginald Maudling, in parliament. She lost her seat in 1974.
Roisin McAliskey's supporters plan to demonstrate outside Holloway prison on Saturday to call for her release.
